title: Compare EMD vs binned Poisson NLL loss with reparam + analytic regulator
description:
Active loss in zcat.update() is compute_earthmovers_distance (triangular-kernel weighted EMD on normalized CDFs). The original motivation was to add depth near the global minimum, which was historically very flat. Replace/compare with a true binned Poisson NLL: -2*sum_i [mu_i - n_i + n_i*log(n_i/mu_i)] where mu_i is the MC template scaled to data. Likelihood curvature scales linearly with N_events per bin, so near the minimum the Poisson NLL is steeper than EMD on normalized CDFs (EMD saturates as N->inf). Additionally test two orthogonal sharpening levers that preserve the statistical interpretation: (a) reparametrize the scales as log(alpha) so the Hessian is more uniform around alpha~1, and (b) add a small Gaussian regulator sum (alpha_i - 1)^2/sigma_prior^2 with sigma_prior chosen so the prior dominates only when likelihood is flat (e.g. sigma_prior = 0.05). Compare on the same step4 input: (i) recovered scales/smearings, (ii) per-cat NLL curvature at minimum (numerical Hessian), (iii) bias from the --test-method-accuracy harness over a toy ensemble (see ecal-ss for toy-ensemble ticket if filed), (iv) AdamW iterations to convergence.

## Context
Historical reason for EMD: provide depth near the flat global minimum. Physical reason for tail downweighting (now subject of separate ticket): off-shell Z events in tails are poorly modeled. See conversation 2026-05-23 review for full discussion.
acceptance_criteria: Notebook or script that runs the four configurations (EMD baseline, Poisson, Poisson+log-reparam, Poisson+log-reparam+regulator) on a representative step4 input and a closure config. Produces: comparison table of recovered values, Hessian eigenvalues, and convergence iterations; pull distributions from N>=200 toys per configuration. Decision documented (which loss becomes default; whether the others stay behind a CLI flag).

title: Off-diagonal category weighting: replace 0.1 magic constant with normalized scheme
description:
zcat.__init__ sets self.weight = 1 for diagonal cats (i==j) and 0.1 for off-diagonal cats. The 0.1 is a magic number with no documented justification beyond 'penalize off-diagonal fits'. Replace with a scheme that makes the relative diag/off-diag contribution explicit and configurable. Two candidate schemes to evaluate: (A) Sum-normalized: scale all off-diagonal weights so that sum_{off-diag} weight = ratio * sum_{diag} weight, with ratio configurable (default 1.0 or 0.5). This removes the arbitrary 0.1 and makes the diag/off-diag balance independent of how many off-diagonals there are. (B) Stats-weighted: each off-diag weight proportional to sqrt(N_cat) (or 1/sigma_cat^2 if per-cat uncertainties are available), then sum-normalize as in (A). This protects against a high-stats off-diag being drowned by a low-stats off-diag that happens to have the same nominal weight. Implement (A) as the default; provide a CLI flag for the ratio; benchmark (B) and decide whether it justifies the extra complexity.

## Context
User: 'I dont have a good solution for what kind of knob this needs to be or what order of magnitude the off-diagonals are contributing over the diagonals. Perhaps it would be better just to normalize the sum(off-diagonal) to the same scale as sum(diagonal)?' — that suggestion is option (A) above.
acceptance_criteria: New MinimizationConfig field off_diag_weight_ratio (default chosen to roughly reproduce current behavior; document the equivalent ratio). zcat construction reads this. CLI flag --off-diag-ratio. Closure run reproduces current values within statistical noise at the chosen default. Stats-weighted variant is implemented behind a flag with comparison results documented.
close_reason: Implemented in b69f139. Default 'constant' scheme with 0.1 preserves legacy behavior bit-for-bit. 'sum-normalized' scheme available via --off-diag-weight-scheme. Follow-up: instrument and decide if 'stat-weighted' is worth implementing (see off-diag-weight-rationale memory).

title: Replace EMD triangular tail downweighting with hard fit window
description:
compute_earthmovers_distance + build_emd_weights apply a triangular kernel (floor 0.1) across the Z mass histogram bins to suppress the off-shell Z tails. The physics motivation is real (off-shell DY/Z production is poorly modeled, especially in highly off-diagonal categories), but a soft per-bin kernel is hard to justify and hard to vary as a systematic. Replace with an explicit hard mass window applied at histogram construction time: only bins fully contained in [hist_min_eff, hist_max_eff] enter the loss. Defaults: 80-100 GeV (matches DataConstants MIN/MAX_INVMASS). Expose hist_min_eff/hist_max_eff in MinimizationConfig + CLI so the window can be varied as a systematic. This also eliminates the build_emd_weights / _emd_weights precomputation entirely.

## Context
User explicitly motivates: 'minimize the impact non-agreement in the tails has on the overall value of the scales and smearings'. The trade-off (less smearing sensitivity in tails) is accepted. Hard window is more defensible and easier to vary for systematics studies.
acceptance_criteria: Hard window replaces triangular kernel. New CLI flags --fit-window-min/--fit-window-max wired through MinimizationConfig. Run with default 80-100 reproduces (within statistical noise) the current values for at least one closure config. Document expected systematic from window variation (e.g. +/-2 GeV) in a follow-up note. Old build_emd_weights / _emd_weights code is removed if loss converges; if Poisson NLL ticket lands first, apply the same window machinery there.
close_reason: Implemented in 988a914. Default flipped from triangular kernel to uniform (hard window). hist_min/hist_max already define the window. Triangular weighting retained behind --loss-weighting triangular. Will change derived values within statistical noise vs prior runs (acceptance criterion).

title: Profile target_function smart-skip caching under AdamW
description:
The 'smart skip' logic in target_function_wrapper (python/helpers/helper_minimizer.py L62-L89) maintains previous_guess[0] = last-call x, and target_function only re-runs zcat.update() for categories whose indices changed between successive calls. This is well-suited to coordinate descent or L-BFGS-B (which probes one coordinate at a time during finite-difference Jacobian estimation), but the AdamW path in python/utilities/adamw_minimizer.py computes a central-difference gradient by alternating fun(x_fwd) and fun(x_bwd) for every coordinate i in sequence. Because x_fwd and x_bwd each differ from the previous call in (typically) only one index but x_fwd[i] != x_bwd[i-1] in general, the set of 'changed' indices may be larger than necessary and the cache hit rate is probably much lower than under L-BFGS-B. Worth measuring before deciding whether to (a) drop the wrapper, (b) extend it with a small key->result LRU keyed on (lead_idx, sublead_idx, x[lead], x[sublead], x[smear_lead], x[smear_sub]), or (c) push caching into zcat.update itself.

## Context
See conversation 2026-05-23 review for full context. Cross-ref: python/utilities/adamw_minimizer.py finite-difference loop and python/helpers/helper_minimizer.py target_function.
acceptance_criteria: Profile a representative step4 minimization with AdamW. Report: (1) total fun() calls, (2) total zcat.update() calls, (3) fraction of zcat.update() calls that would have been skipped if results were cached on the per-cat parameter tuple, (4) wall-clock breakdown for numba histogram vs. EMD vs. python overhead. Decide on (a/b/c) above based on numbers and either implement or document why no change is needed.
close_reason: Profiled in 02c0702 (notes/adamw-cache-profile.md). Measured 57.94% skip rate under AdamW vs 48.83% under L-BFGS-B — cache is MORE effective under AdamW than originally feared. Recommendation: keep as-is. Estimated upside of per-cat value caching is only 15-20%, not worth the complexity.

title: Wire up CLI flags for minimizer bounds
description:
set_bounds in python/helpers/helper_minimizer.py hardcodes bounds (0.96, 1.04) for scales and (0.0, 0.05) for smearings across most branches; closure has its own (0.99, 1.01) / (0.95, 1.05). The user noted there may already be partial CLI plumbing for this that isn't wired up — investigate that first before adding new flags. Add (or wire up): --scale-bounds MIN MAX, --smear-bounds MIN MAX, with separate --closure-scale-bounds. Defaults reproduce current behavior exactly. Plumb through MinimizationConfig so the dataclass owns the values and set_bounds just reads them.

## Context
User: physically scales shouldn't exceed +/-4%, but flag is still useful for special studies; suspects partial wiring already exists. Look at helper_pymin.get_options first.
acceptance_criteria: CLI flags exist and override defaults. MinimizationConfig has scale_bounds / smear_bounds / closure_scale_bounds fields. set_bounds reads from config; the conditional structure (closure / test-method-accuracy / fix-scales / default) is preserved. Existing scripts/ invocations continue to produce identical bounds without modification. Test covering at least the default and a custom override.
close_reason: Implemented in 38c1e54. Defaults exactly preserve prior behavior; verified with 5 scenarios (default, closure, closure-wide, fix-scales, override).

title: Per-category RNG seed for smearing draws
description:
zcat.__init__ uses self.seed = 3543136929 (a single hardcoded seed) for every category's smearing draws (_generate_smearing_randn). Using the same seed across categories correlates the smearing realizations between unrelated dielectron categories — fluctuations that should be independent are not. Switch to a per-category seed derived deterministically from the category indices, e.g. seed = (3543136929 ^ (lead_index * 1315423911) ^ (sublead_index * 2654435761)) & 0xFFFFFFFF, so reproducibility is preserved but the draws are independent across categories. Keep the base seed configurable via MinimizationConfig (and CLI) for future toy-ensemble work.

## Context
Cheap change; user agreed in 2026-05-23 review.
acceptance_criteria: zcat seed derived from (lead_index, sublead_index) + a base seed. Base seed exposed via MinimizationConfig with sensible default matching current 3543136929. Closure/test-method-accuracy runs are still bit-reproducible for a fixed base seed. Optional: smoke test verifies that two distinct cats with same (smear values, mc events) produce different smeared outputs.
close_reason: Implemented in 77a6c4d. _derive_cat_seed mixes base seed with (lead_index, sublead_index) via Knuth-style XOR; deterministic and independent across cats.

value: target_function smart-skip cache (helper_minimizer.target_function_wrapper) compares the current guess to previous_guess[0] and skips zcat.update() for unchanged scale indices. Designed for L-BFGS-B style coordinate probes where one parameter changes at a time. The current default minimizer is AdamW (DataConstants.MINIMIZATION_STRATEGY), which does central finite differences — every iteration probes 2n points where typically all n coordinates differ between consecutive evaluations, defeating the cache. See ticket ecal-ss-nx4 to profile and either restore the per-coordinate skip or replace with a true per-(cat,scale_index) memoization.

Bounds rationale: helper_minimizer.set_bounds hardcodes scales in (0.96, 1.04) — physically residual scales cannot exceed +/-4% even for early-data / transition regions. The CLI flag (ticket ecal-ss-pdh) is for convenience and systematic studies, not because the default is unsafe.

Minimization surface shape: globally relatively smooth (per user's historical exploration), but extremely flat near the global minimum. This is the root motivation for both the dead nll*chi_sqr loss and the current EMD loss. Any new loss must be evaluated on its near-minimum curvature, not just its global behavior. log(alpha) reparametrization + analytic Gaussian regulator are the canonical statistical-physics fixes; multiplying by chi^2 is not.

Loss function lineage: original loss was -2*(nll+penalty)*chi_sqr (compute_nll_chisqr in zcat_class.py) — motivated by need for steeper minimum surface, but chi^2 multiplication breaks statistical interpretation. Current active loss is compute_earthmovers_distance with triangular kernel (build_emd_weights). Triangular kernel downweights Z mass tails because off-shell Z production is poorly modeled and statistics are low in off-diagonal cats — this is intentional, accepted trade-off vs smearing sensitivity in the tails. compute_nll_chisqr is now effectively dead code.

Off-diagonal weight: zcat.__init__ sets weight=1 for i==j else 0.1. The 0.1 is undocumented. User has no measurement of how much off-diagonals actually contribute to the total loss vs diagonals — that measurement is a prerequisite for picking a defensible scheme (ticket ecal-ss-e31). When implementing, first instrument current behavior to log sum(diag) vs sum(off-diag) per iteration for at least one representative step.

Smearing model is multiplicative Gaussian on energy with a single rho per category (zcat_class.py _smear_energies). The simplicity is dictated by available statistical power, not by physics — a richer model (e.g. double-Gaussian / asymmetric) would be under-constrained per cat. Important consequence: smearings CANNOT be derived as a compounding step-to-step correction; they must be re-derived in full at each step. Step5 ('stochastic') workflows are bolted on top of this, not natively supported by the core minimizer.

time_stability.py L80-96 uses median(m_ee)/TARGET_MASS per (run-bin, eta-bin) and silently falls back to 1.0 when N<2 events. User has tried fits and they fail in hard-to-debug ways; median is robust. Recommended middle ground if anyone revisits: fit when N>few-thousand AND fit converges, fall back to median otherwise, RECORD which path was taken in the output file so downstream consumers can see which bins used the fallback.

MC oversampling in data_loader.py (~L290) doubles the MC array via np.append. This LOOKS like a no-op but is intentional: smearing draws inside zcat are independent per replica, so the doubled MC is effectively a coarse MC integration over the smearing kernel — smooths the smeared response in each bin. Do not 'optimize' this away. Should be commented in-code; see ticket backlog.
